chapter: Wingy Manone and Bix in Chicago (draft typing)
title: Augie the drummer quits over talk of seances
summary: Hodes recalls a drummer, Augie, who was dour and overheard band talk about reincarnation and seances. He packed his drums in the middle of the night and went to work as a bartender. Years later the same talk came up in a car with Earl Murphy.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: In fact, I never heard soloing on drums, outside of Baby Dodds, doing the things he did. I never heard soloing in those days. The drummer played drums for the band. You didn't take no breaks. And here is Augie, just laying down that beat, and -- let's get it going, maybe it'll take us two hours, to hit that beautiful groove where the world could come to an end and it doesn't matter.

Because you're into it, you understand. So -- and now he's exposed on the bandstand. When the music is -- when somebody is laying out and Harvey is talking to the boys about, when you're done you don't die, because you go on. And you change bodies and -- but you go on. And these things -- maybe I believe it now, but at that time, -- for for Augie, and it was the fourth night, we just started playing. And Augie was not the kind of guy that you could talk to. He was dour, that kind of -- I mean, you would have to go in a room and take a quiet time and say, well, is this the moment I should broach the subject? You didn't know how he was going to react.

Musically, fine. He loved me, we got along real fine. But we didn't have to talk. We played. But he overheard this. And here it is, 9:00, we started and it's 10:00, he's back in his drums. And nobody wants to say anything, ______ doesn't

want to say nothing. And he packs the drums and calls a cab and hauls him out to the South Side, 1800 or somewhere, where some gangsters . . . to go to work as a bartender, which is what he did, and just put the drums down.

And we didn't find out til later what it was, that it was this conversation that was driving him up the wall. And an interesting story about this is that, years later, it was little George . . . that was in the car, and Hillard is in the front with Murphy.

And myself. And George is in the back, and I don't know who he's with. But they were talking about the same subject, about having a seance and all that. Murphy says, what the hell are they talking about? I says, I don't know, they didn't give me any.
